title: Machtir
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Eruvin 53b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.53b.17) they ask Rabbi Ilai, “Tell us where Rabbi Abbahu is hidden.” He answers, “He took counsel with the Machtir.” [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Eruvin.53b.17.1) explains that this means the Nasi; [Rabbeinu Chananel](https://www.sefaria.org/Rabbeinu_Chananel_on_Eruvin.53b.7) explains it as taking counsel with the head of the yeshiva. Hyman accordingly takes it to mean Rabbi Yochanan, his teacher, as also reported in Yuchasin in the name of Rav Tzemach Gaon.

notes.text: Rashi takes Machtir to be the Nasi who grants permission to ordain, while Rabbeinu Chananel reads “head of the yeshiva.” Hyman infers that it refers to Rabbi Yochanan. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2457&lang=en) records Rabbi Yochanan as an interpretation and also reports that some read it as the name of a sage.
